source.title: Beyond Safe Data: Pretraining-Stage Alignment with Regular Safety Reflection
source.authors: Jin-Hao Li; K. Tang; Yi-Han Xu; Zhuorui Ye; Kaifeng Lyu

record.tranche_reason: Tests related safety-erosion and bypass outcomes using pretraining reflections, fine-tuning attacks, and behavioral attack-success measures rather than reproducing the original studies’ methods or measuring per-token KL.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own fine-tuning, prefill, GCG, and reflection-interval results. Related-work descriptions of earlier fine-tuning and first-token findings are cited background, not extracted results. No per-token KL, parameter localization, or direct measurement of how aligned and base output distributions differ by response position is reported.
record.test_reason: The paper reports its own harmful and benign fine-tuning attacks, plus prefill and GCG attacks, on safety-trained 1.7B models and on synthetic 135M models. It also evaluates a deepening method: periodic safety reflections in pretraining and SFT that recur through the whole response, tested against those attacks. It reports no per-token KL, no parameter localization and no analysis of causes, so V3, V5 and V6 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also conclude, from MedSafetyWorld, that safe data alone does not prevent unsafe generalization, so filtering and rewriting are insufficient. SRP's robustness to fine-tuning is claimed only within the closed-source threat model; SRP fails under open-source fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes regular segment-level safety reflections during pretraining and compatible post-training. It does not reproduce harmful/benign fine-tuning as the original intervention or measure per-token KL as in the cited first-token study.
record.method_sensitivity: Reflection placement across pretraining and post-training changes attack outcomes; pretraining-only reflections perform poorly in Table 4. Reflection interval changes results in Table 7. The open-source setting without provider safeguards substantially weakens fine-tuning robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: SRP improves response-level safety classification (unsafe recall 91.22 vs 80.35 for post-train only) and lowers base-model JB-Completions ASR (2.92 vs 9.89).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining-stage reflection improves a model's ability to classify unsafe content.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are given for the reported attack rates. Several interval and epoch-sweep results are presented in figures or qualitative text rather than exact values. Fine-tuning robustness is partly evaluated in a closed-source threat model that retains provider safeguards; the paper itself reports much weaker robustness when those safeguards are removed. The controlled MedSafetyWorld experiments use 135M models.
record.rows_left_out: For Figure 5, omitted separate epoch-by-epoch plotted points; the text-level results are retained for the named fine-tuning outcomes. For Table 7, omitted non-refusal-rate columns and kept the unsafe-compliance measures for each interval. Other capability and safety-classification results were left out because they do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: No sample-count sweep. It is not established that a few to a few hundred examples suffice; Harmful HEx-PHI is fine-tuned over many epochs.
Real-world benign (GSM8K) effect on Baseline and SafeLM is only plotted in Figure 5, with no stated values. Synthetic benign data are reverse-direction safe facts, not ordinary instruction data.
No per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
Does not measure whether safety is spread over token positions; the method is reflection tokens, not the original token-wise constrained objective or data augmentation.

missing.what: SRP-Hint inference attacks: prefill unsafe compliance 0.30 and GCG 0.88/1.10. After benign GSM8K fine-tuning without reflections, ASR rises 0.00 to 33.50.
MedSafetyWorld prefill ASR without vs with pretraining reflection: single-hop 44.20/7.60 (<Safe>), two-hop 25.60/3.60.
Post-train-only reflection is quickly erased under adversarial fine-tuning, while SRP stays robust (qualitative, Figure 7).
Baseline and SafeLM benign GSM8K fine-tuning ASR curves (values only in Figure 5).

record.verdict_notes: Comparator rows for SRP variants were moved from V4 to V7: a low attack rate on a deepened model tests the fix, not the bypass. Fine-tuning robustness relies on provider-side mixing of about 30 SFT samples and a '<think>' template trick. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The synthetic results come from 135M models with a heuristic judge.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report a fine-tuning sample-count sweep or establish that a few to a few hundred harmful examples suffice; it reports fine-tuning attack outcomes and epoch sweeps.
Does not isolate ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning across a stated few-to-hundreds sample range; synthetic benign fine-tuning and GSM8K fine-tuning are tested.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or response-position analysis.
Tests prefilling and GCG suffix attacks, and mentions SafeBeam decoding; does not systematically test other decoding changes.
No weight, neuron, rank, or parameter-localization intervention or measurement.
Does not test whether the data or objective underlying post-training alignment causes first-token concentration or shallowness.
Tests periodic safety reflections and their robustness to attacks, including reflection intervals; does not measure whether safety is distributed across response-token positions.
